<notes>
kept -> inv1 candidate -> no harness changes proposed; inv1 rollout with identical code differs from base1 (gets 13 vs unknown) but this is consistent with LLM sample variance, not a harness defect; inv1 evaluator correctly noted base1 reached a defensible conclusion given its reasoning

kept -> dom1 candidate -> no harness changes proposed; dom1 rollout with identical code also gets 13 (same answer as inv1); dom1 evaluator correctly noted base1 had worked correctly under its reasoning path

The evidence shows: base1 produced "unknown" by concluding that the specific lost extra-extra-large item cannot be identified and thus the count is indeterminate. Both inv1 and dom1 produce "13" by the same harness, through more complete union-counting of the target group. The difference is in LLM reasoning depth, not harness structure. Both candidates confirmed the harness is adequate by proposing no edits. Since both candidates show the identical harness works across independent runs and both evaluators found no basis for edits, the harness is fit for purpose. Base1's "unknown" answer reflects incomplete LLM reasoning (failure to recognize that ALL extra-extra-large items, by definition of being extra-extra-large, satisfy one of the target criteria), not a failure of harness design. No structural change to the harness is supported by the evidence.
</notes>
